clips.title: The story
paras: Camping 101: First Aid is an instructional quest that sends skilled travelers to Rawrk in Razor Hill, who teaches them how to craft their own First Aid Kit for wilderness survival. It emphasizes the necessities of self-reliance on the trail, reminding adventurers to master campfire creation and respect local settlements by camping out in the wild.

Survival in the untamed expanses of Durotar and beyond requires more than just raw martial strength; it demands self-sufficiency on the trail. In Razor Hill, Rawrk offers instruction to capable wanderers seeking to fashion essential wilderness gear. Through Camping 101: First Aid, practitioners who have proven their basic proficiency learn to assemble a dedicated First Aid Kit, giving them the means to mend wounds and tend to injuries far from the safety of an apothecary or infirmary.

Setting up camp is an art governed by practical frontier etiquette and necessity. Rawrk cautions adventurers that pitching tents in the center of settlements like Razor Hill is unwelcome, meaning these wilderness stations must be tested out in the open wilds. Furthermore, no campsite is functional without a roaring campfire to stave off the night, making a passing familiarity with the culinary arts—where firemaking is first mastered—a vital asset for any prospective camper.

clips.title: Quest text
paras: So you've taken up First Aid? That's an honorable... And pragmatic pursuit as an adventurer.

I reckon I know someone that can teach you how to craft a First Aid Kit for your camp. Injuries are a reality in the world of adventuring and offering some much-needed healing at your camp could even save lives.

clips.title: Completion
paras: There you have it, you can now craft your very own First Aid Kit. Most folk don't care much for camps being set up in the center of town, so you'll need to head into the wilderness if you want to test it out.

Oh, and just remember, no camp is complete without a campfire. You'll need one of those before you start up your camp. Most cooks can teach you to make a fire. If you haven't already, you might want to check in with someone who can train you in the culinary arts to learn the basics.
